key_concept: Bacteria are classified by shape into four groups: spherical cocci, rod-shaped bacilli, comma-shaped vibrio and spiral spirilla.
steps: A. Spherical: spherical bacteria are called cocci (singular coccus), so A matches II.
B. Rod: rod-shaped bacteria are called bacilli (singular bacillus), so B matches IV.
C. Comma: comma-shaped bacteria are called vibrio, for example *Vibrio cholerae*, so C matches I.
D. Spirillum: spiral-shaped bacteria are called spirilla (singular spirillum), so D matches III.
The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which is option (4).
why_not_others: Option (3) gets A right but wrongly pairs Rod with Vibrio and Comma with Bacilli. Options (1) and (2) fail at once because they do not match Spherical with Cocci.
common_trap: Students mix up vibrio (comma-shaped, a curved rod) with bacilli (straight rod) because both are rod-like.
time_saving_tip: Spherical-Cocci (II) eliminates options (1) and (2). Comma-Vibrio (I) then picks option (4) over option (3).
